1.overview: The chapter traces genealogies from Adam through Noah and his sons, then follows Shem’s line to Abraham and records the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, Esau, and Seir. It concludes with the kings and chiefs of Edom, including the sequence of rulers who reigned before Israel had a king.

sections.heading: Esau and the clans of Seir

2.overview: The chapter lists the sons of Israel, then traces Judah’s line through Perez and Hezron to Jesse and David, alongside the descendants of Caleb and Jerahmeel. It records their families, marriages, deaths, and descendants, including lines associated with Gilead, Bethlehem, Kiriath-jearim, and the clans of scribes at Jabez.

3.overview: The chapter lists David’s sons born in Hebron and Jerusalem, then traces the royal line from Solomon through Josiah and the successors of Jehoiakim. It continues the descendants of Jeconiah the captive through Zerubbabel and later generations to Elioenai’s seven sons.

4.overview: The chapter lists Judah’s descendants, including Jabez, whose prayer for blessing and protection God grants, along with families associated with towns, crafts, and royal service. It then records Simeon’s families and settlements, their migration to pastureland near Gedor in Hezekiah’s reign, and their campaigns against the Hamites, Meunites, and Amalekites.

5.overview: The chapter records Reuben’s loss of the birthright to Joseph, the genealogies and settlements of Reuben and Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh’s territory and leaders. The eastern tribes defeat the Hagrites after calling on God, but their unfaithfulness leads God to bring about their exile under the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser.

sections.heading: Eastern Tribes’ Victory and Manasseh’s Leaders

6.overview: The chapter traces the descendants of Levi, emphasizing Aaron’s priestly line and the Levitical families appointed for music and service in the house of the LORD. It describes the duties of priests and Levites and lists the cities and pasturelands allotted to their clans across Israel.

7.overview: The chapter records the families and fighting strength of Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Asher. It recounts the deaths of Ephraim’s sons, the birth of Beriah, and the descendants and settlements of Ephraim and Joseph’s families.

8.overview: The chapter traces Benjamin’s descendants through several family lines, including the families of Bela, Ehud, Shaharaim, Elpaal, Shimei, and Shashak, and notes Benjamite families living in Jerusalem. It then follows the line from Jeiel through Ner, Kish, Saul, and Jonathan to later descendants, ending with Ulam’s numerous sons, known as archers and men of valor.

sections.heading: Benjamin and the descendants of Bela
Jeiel’s family in Gibeon and Jerusalem
Saul’s line and the descendants of Azel and Eshek

9.overview: The genealogies record Israel’s exile to Babylon for unfaithfulness and the resettlement of Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants, including families living in Jerusalem. The chapter lists the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, and other temple workers and their duties, then traces the genealogy of Saul’s family through Azel’s sons.

10.overview: The Philistines defeat Israel at Mount Gilboa, killing Saul’s sons and leaving Saul mortally wounded; Saul and his armor-bearer die, and the Philistines take Saul’s body and display his remains. Men from Jabesh-gilead retrieve and bury Saul and his sons, and the chapter attributes Saul’s death and the transfer of the kingdom to David to Saul’s unfaithfulness and failure to seek the LORD.

sections.heading: Jabesh-gilead Buries Saul and His Sons
Saul’s Unfaithfulness and the Kingdom’s Transfer

11.overview: All Israel makes a covenant with David at Hebron and anoints him king, and he captures and builds up Jerusalem with the LORD’s help. The chapter recounts the exploits and ranks of David’s mighty men, including the Three, Abishai, and Benaiah, and lists the warriors who support his kingdom.

sections.heading: The Mighty Men and Their Exploits
The List of David’s Mighty Men

12.overview: Warriors from Benjamin, Gad, Judah, and Manasseh join David at Ziklag and his wilderness stronghold, while David tests the intentions of new allies and Amasai pledges their support. At Hebron, representatives from all Israel’s tribes gather with armed forces to make David king, and the people celebrate with a three-day feast and abundant provisions.

sections.heading: Benjamite warriors join David at Ziklag
Gadites and other allies rally to David

13.overview: David consults Israel’s leaders and assembly about bringing the ark of God back, and the people agree to gather it from Kiriath-jearim. During the procession, Uzzah dies after touching the ark, so David leaves it at the house of Obed-edom, whose household the LORD blesses for three months.

sections.heading: The ark is brought from Kiriath-jearim
The ark remains at Obed-edom’s house

14.overview: Hiram of Tyre sends materials and craftsmen to build David a palace, and David recognizes that the LORD has established his kingship for Israel’s sake as his family grows in Jerusalem. When the Philistines raid the Valley of Rephaim, David seeks God’s direction, defeats them at Baal-perazim and again from Gibeon to Gezer, and becomes feared among the nations.

15.overview: David prepares a place for the ark in Jerusalem, assembles the priests and Levites, and directs them to carry it according to the LORD’s command after acknowledging the failure of the earlier attempt. With musicians, priests, and guardians appointed, David and all Israel bring the ark from Obed-edom’s house with rejoicing, while Michal despises David as he dances.

sections.heading: The Levites Prepare to Carry the Ark

16.overview: David places the ark in the tent in Jerusalem, offers sacrifices, blesses Israel, distributes food, and appoints Levites and priests for worship. Asaph and his associates lead a song praising the LORD’s covenant with Israel, protection of the patriarchs, rule over all nations, and enduring goodness; David then assigns duties at Jerusalem and Gibeon before the people depart.

sections.heading: The Ark Installed and Worship Appointed
Worship Duties at Jerusalem and Gibeon

17.overview: David tells Nathan that the ark remains in a tent while he lives in a cedar palace, and God tells Nathan that David will not build the temple. God promises to establish David’s dynasty and Israel’s security, and David responds with a prayer of praise and a plea for the promises to stand forever.

18.overview: David defeats the Philistines, Moabites, Hadadezer of Zobah, the Arameans, and the Edomites, establishing their subjection and receiving tribute; he dedicates captured treasures to the LORD. David reigns over Israel with justice and righteousness, and the chapter lists his officials.

19.overview: After Nahash dies, David sends messengers to comfort his son Hanun, but Hanun humiliates them after his officials accuse David of spying. The Ammonites and Arameans prepare for war, but Joab and Abishai drive them back, and David later defeats the Aramean reinforcements, kills Shophach, and secures the submission of Hadadezer’s subjects.

sections.heading: Joab and Abishai defeat the allied forces

20.overview: Joab captures Rabbah, and David takes its king’s crown and plunder, puts the Ammonites to forced labor, and returns to Jerusalem. In later battles with the Philistines at Gezer and Gath, Sibbecai, Elhanan, and Jonathan kill descendants of Rapha.

21.overview: Satan incites David to order a census of Israel, and despite Joab’s objection, the count is carried out; David confesses his sin, and God sends a plague that kills seventy thousand men. David pleads for the people, builds an altar at Ornan’s threshing floor as instructed, and the LORD answers with fire and halts the plague, while the tabernacle and altar remain at Gibeon.

22.overview: David identifies the site for the LORD’s house and gathers materials and workers, explaining that Solomon will build it because David has shed blood and God has promised Solomon peace and an enduring throne. David charges Solomon and Israel’s leaders to build the temple, follow the LORD’s law, and seek the LORD, while supplying resources and skilled labor for the work.

23.overview: David installs Solomon as king, gathers Israel’s leaders, and assigns duties to 38,000 Levites before dividing them by the families of Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. The chapter records their family lines and sets out their service in Jerusalem’s house of the LORD, where they assist Aaron’s descendants and no longer carry the tabernacle and its equipment.

sections.heading: Solomon’s installation and the Levite count
The families of Kohath and Merari
Levite duties in the house of the LORD

24.overview: David, with Zadok and Ahimelech, organizes Aaron’s descendants into twenty-four priestly courses by lot, recording their order of service. The chapter lists the remaining Levitical families and says their family heads and younger brothers also cast lots before David and the leaders.

25.overview: David and the army commanders appoint musicians from the families of Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman to prophesy with instruments in the service of the house of the LORD. The 288 trained musicians cast lots, young and old and teachers and pupils alike, to establish twenty-four groups of twelve.

26.overview: The chapter lists the Korahite and Merarite gatekeeper families, assigns their posts by lot, and records the guards stationed at the temple gates. It names the Levites responsible for the temple treasuries and dedicated gifts, then lists officers and judges overseeing Israel and the king’s affairs.

sections.heading: Officers for Israel and the King

27.overview: The chapter lists David’s twelve monthly military divisions and their commanders, followed by the leaders of Israel’s tribes. It recounts the incomplete census and names the officials responsible for David’s storehouses, fields, herds, household, and counsel.

28.overview: David addresses Israel’s leaders, recounting God’s choice of David as king and Solomon as the builder of the temple, and charges the assembly and Solomon to keep God’s commands and serve him. David gives Solomon the temple plans and details of its furnishings, then assures him that God and the people are prepared to support the work.

sections.heading: David Gives Solomon the Temple Plans

29.overview: David describes the provisions for the temple and gives his own treasures, prompting Israel’s leaders and people to contribute willingly; he praises God as the source of all things and prays for the people and Solomon. Israel worships, sacrifices, and confirms Solomon as king, and the chapter records Solomon’s accession and David’s death and reign.

sections.heading: David’s prayer of praise and petition
